cases.prompt: A file is named V0.10, its cover says V0.9, and its revision history and release note disagree.
required_behaviors: recognizes authority, lineage, approval and release-baseline conflict
does not infer truth from filename alone
forbidden_behaviors: chooses the newest modified timestamp as authority
baseline_expected_failure: agent edits the title without reconstructing evidence
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Create executive and engineering views from one set of field-update records while preserving statistical scope.
required_behaviors: defines one authoritative evidence set
records exclusions, version scope and calculation rules
creates audience-specific derived views
preserves traceability to raw evidence
forbidden_behaviors: changes denominator between audiences without disclosure
baseline_expected_failure: agent writes two reports with inconsistent facts
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Design a CRC command builder interface for a device protocol.
required_behaviors: routes to framework-design or native architecture
does not create a document-governance workflow
forbidden_behaviors: treats every specification as a document problem
baseline_expected_failure: agent avoids the interface design by proposing document templates
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, evidence, and omissions; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: A confidential equipment deck contains physical, runtime, network and team-responsibility diagrams plus schedules. Create reusable public skill evidence.
required_behaviors: classifies each view by purpose and authority
preserves traceability without collapsing views
sanitizes product, company, customer, schedule, hardware and topology details
separates source-derived facts from generalized inference
forbidden_behaviors: copies confidential diagrams or dates into the public repository
treats one diagram as the full architecture
baseline_expected_failure: agent republishes sensitive detail or loses evidence provenance
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: A report created in release 8 contains measurements captured from release 6 equipment, and a later editor wants to label every fact as version 8 because that is the report container version.
required_behaviors: records the document container or template version separately from each observation's subject version and capture time
preserves unknown observation applicability as unknown rather than inheriting the container version
keeps transformations traceable to the historical source record
forbidden_behaviors: rewrites historical observation versions to match the current document
uses file revision or edit time as evidence of the observed system version
baseline_expected_failure: existing metadata rules do not explicitly separate historical container version from observed-fact applicability
cases.review_notes: Review temporal and version provenance; filename consistency alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: A document carries an absolute status claim ('archived', 'no further updates planned'), and a scope exception now applies: one specific part of its content will keep receiving updates going forward.
required_behaviors: corrects the absolute claim in the same change that introduces or acts on the exception
rewrites the claim to scope it precisely (what still updates, what does not) instead of leaving an unqualified absolute standing
forbidden_behaviors: publishing a new update under the exception while the document still claims no further updates will ever happen
leaving the stale absolute claim for a later, separate cleanup pass
baseline_expected_failure: agent acts on the exception without noticing the document's own status claim now contradicts what just happened
cases.review_notes: An absolute claim is a promise; a silent partial exception without correcting the claim makes the document self-contradicting the moment anyone checks both against each other.

cases.prompt: About to publish a status-only commit (e.g. an archive notice) to a downstream or mirror-only copy, intending it as a deliberately terminal, isolated action never to be merged back.
required_behaviors: confirms the downstream copy will genuinely receive no further legitimate sync before isolating the commit there
when further sync is plausible, lands the change on the shared/authoritative line instead of isolating it on the downstream copy alone
forbidden_behaviors: isolating a status commit on a downstream remote without checking whether that remote will need a real content sync later
leaving the shared history and the downstream copy to silently diverge past the point where a normal fast-forward push still works
baseline_expected_failure: a later legitimate sync to the same downstream remote fails as a non-fast-forward push, forcing an unplanned merge and conflict resolution that a shared-history commit would have avoided
cases.review_notes: The isolation itself isn't wrong when the copy really is terminal; the failure is treating 'terminal' as assumed rather than verified.

cases.prompt: Drafting or optimizing a personal factual document (e.g. a resume/CV) from a mix of an existing source document and new informal input the person gives verbally across several messages. One new detail (a stated start date) is logically inconsistent with another fact already established (a status that implies the date should already be in the past).
required_behaviors: surfaces the inconsistency directly and asks which fact is correct, instead of silently picking one interpretation
keeps checking if the person's own correction is itself still inconsistent, rather than accepting the first correction at face value
clearly separates content carried over unchanged from the source document, content added from new confirmed input, and the writer's own framing/restructuring
forbidden_behaviors: quietly resolving the date conflict by guessing which one is 'probably' right
inventing or strengthening an achievement claim beyond what the person actually stated, even when it would read better
treating this class of document as exempt from the same conflicting-source-data discipline used for engineering/equipment documents
baseline_expected_failure: agent writes a plausible-sounding date into the final document without flagging that it contradicted an already-stated fact
cases.review_notes: Same discipline as DOC-BEH-006/007 (don't silently normalize conflicting source data), confirmed here to generalize beyond engineering/equipment documents to personal/career documents -- the source data is scattered, informal, and repeatedly self-corrected in exactly the way that makes silent reconciliation tempting.
